newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba council meets, no rate changes expected.
newsitem.headline: Buba council meets, no rate changes expected.

text.p: Germany's Bundesbank council began its fortnightly meeting on Thursday amid expectations it would keep its three key interest rates steady.
Last week's U.S. interest rate hike has not triggered a rise in the dollar, German inflation remains subdued and economic expansion is weak, arguing against a rate increase.
Money supply growth, on the other hand, remains above the central bank's target range, arguing against a cut in rates.
A central bank official confirmed that the meeting had begun. No news conference is scheduled after the meeting.

"The German economy is moving forward only with great effort," the Association of German Banks said in a report this week. "It is hardly to be feared that the Bundesbank will pull in the monetary policy reins this year."

The dollar's sharp rise in the past six months raises the spectre of imported inflation by increasing the prices of dollar-denominated goods. But that potential has hardly been translated into reality.
And last week's 25 basis point rise in the U.S. federal funds rate has not further bolstered the dollar, which has trended downward to the current 1.68 marks from 1.71 marks a month ago.
Economists polled by Reuters earlier this week unanimously predicted the Bundesbank would not move to change German interest rates.

The discount rate has been at a historic low 2.5 percent since last April, while the Lombard rate stands at 4.5 percent. The main money market rate, the securities repurchase rate, has been steady at 3.0 percent since last August.
At this week's securities repurchase tender, the central bank drained 2.9 billion marks as cash returned to the money market following the Easter holiday.
